evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:22 — must fix the res/response bug and use the dead ApiError at api.ts:4
app/src/lib/api.ts:25 — must evict rejected promises from the cache
app/src/lib/components.ts:43 + 5 route sites — must consolidate the not-found markup and delete sectionHeading
app/src/routes/(home).ts:60-62 — must reuse idFromUrl/isSpeciesId
app/src/document.ts:12-13 — must switch to the documented project-root asset paths
app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:16 — must separate 404 from upstream errors
review_cost.rationale: A full round of changes before approving, but every item is small, local and mechanical — nothing structural would need rework.

findings.issue: The non-OK branch throws `HTTP ${res.status} ${res.statusText}` but the parameter is `response`; every failed API request throws ReferenceError: res is not defined. The ApiError class (api.ts:4-8) was written for this and is never used.
findings.suggestion: Throw `new ApiError(response.status, url)` (or at minimum use `response.status`), and delete or use ApiError consistently.

findings.issue: Rejected promises are cached in the module-level Map forever, so a transient API failure (or a 404 for a resource that is added later, which the spec explicitly anticipates) remains broken until process restart; the cache is also unbounded.
findings.suggestion: Evict the cache entry when the promise rejects (`request.catch(() => cache.delete(url))`) and consider an LRU/TTL bound for large payloads.

findings.issue: getMoveDetailsForGame silently filters out moves whose detail fetch failed, so rows vanish from the moves tables with no error surfaced (compounded by the sticky rejection cache).
findings.suggestion: Distinguish 404s (drop the row) from transient errors (fail the page render), and log the dropped move.

findings.issue: `.catch(() => null)` conflates upstream API errors with genuine not-found, serving a 404 page (and 404 status) when the API is down or erroring; tryApi does the same in the other detail routes.
findings.suggestion: Only map a 404 status to the not-found page; propagate other failures to Gracile's error handler (500).

findings.issue: Stylesheet and client-script URLs are built with `new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname` instead of the documented convention of project-root paths (`/src/document.client.ts`), relying on implicit Vite build-time rewriting.
findings.suggestion: Use the documented form: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/document.css">` and `<script type="module" src="/src/document.client.ts">`.

findings.issue: A shared notFound() helper exists unused while the same not-found markup is copy-pasted in five places (pokemon/[name].ts:55, moves/[name].ts:31, abilities/[name].ts:33, types/[name].ts:29, 404.ts:11), so a wording change requires five edits.
findings.suggestion: Use the helper everywhere (or a tiny fragment route) and delete the copies; also delete the unused sectionHeading (components.ts:50).

findings.issue: Re-implements idFromUrl/isSpeciesId inline with a fresh regex instead of importing the existing helpers from lib/api.ts:32-40.
`Number(detail?.order ?? idFromUrl(ref.url) ?? 0)` can produce NaN because ?? doesn't catch NaN from idFromUrl, corrupting the version-group sort.
findings.suggestion: Use `Number.isFinite` on the fallback, e.g. `const n = detail?.order ?? idFromUrl(ref.url); return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : 0`.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent on a malformed param (e.g. `/pokemon/%`) throws URIError, which Gracile's middleware converts to a 500 instead of the spec's not-found page.
findings.suggestion: Wrap decode in a try/catch (or validate the param) and return the 404 branch on failure.

findings.issue: Every API response is typed `any` (api<T = any> call sites never pass T), so the external PokeAPI contract — the app's main integration surface — is untyped.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the consumed shapes (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, generation) and pass them to api<T>.

summary: This is a competent, genuinely idiomatic Gracile 0.11 SSR app: documented route conventions, the official Hono adapter, clean handler→props→template flow and a tidy server/client split. The merge blockers are concentrated in the API client — an undefined-variable bug in the error path, permanently cached rejected promises that silently drop or misclassify data, and 404/error conflation — plus copy-pasted not-found markup and untyped API shapes. Fixable in one focused round; I'd approve after that round.
